title: Ivo and the Echo
premise: Edmund Blackwood, a forensic actuary who investigates 'impossible' insurance claims, is sent to audit the colony world of Vesper-9, officially decommissioned and forgotten. There he finds survivors who shouldn't exist, including Ivo, a child born after the colony's supposed evacuation, who carries implanted memories of a massacre the corporate archives have erased. As Edmund reconstructs the truth from corrupted manifests and living testimony, he realizes his own employer orchestrated both the atrocity and its erasure—and that his own past on Vesper-9 was surgically removed. In the end, Edmund chooses loyalty to the dead over duty to the living corporation, broadcasting the recovered records at the cost of his identity, while Ivo escapes carrying the echo of everything they lost.
about_author: C. M. Ishikawa is a former maritime claims adjuster turned novelist who writes quiet, devastating science fiction about paperwork and grief. They live in a coastal town where they keep meticulous records of ships that never arrived.

chapters.title: The Actuary of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Introduce him as an investigator whose specialty is claims that defy physics—deaths that never happened, ships that never flew. He receives an anomalous file: a life-insurance payout for someone listed as deceased on a colony that officially has no graves. Emotional beat: lonely competence masking a hollow he can't name.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He traces the manifest anomaly to the Meridian Dawn, a transport with no flight logs, no crew roster, and one impossible passenger name: Ivo. His request for records triggers a silent corporate alarm. Beat: first crack in the seamless world; unease sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Vesper-9, Population Zero
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He arrives at the officially abandoned colony expecting ruins and finds greenhouses still breathing, power still humming, and fresh footprints in regolith dust. Someone is living where no one is. Beat: wonder curdling into dread—the lie is being maintained by someone active.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Wasn't Born
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He meets Ivo, a twelve-year-old survivor who knows Edmund's name before it's spoken. Ivo claims to remember things that happened before his birth. Beat: uncanny connection; Edmund's professional detachment begins to fail him.

chapters.title: Memories on Loan
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Inside Ivo's mind: implanted memories of the massacre night—sirens, sealed doors, his mother's voice saying run. He doesn't know which memories are his own. Beat: disorientation and grief; the reader sees the horror firsthand through borrowed eyes.

chapters.title: The Quiet Ledger
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the colony archive he finds a handwritten ledger kept by the dead—a secret census of 4,112 souls the official record says were evacuated safely. Cross-referencing shows 4,112 people who never arrived anywhere. Beat: cold fury; proof begins to take shape.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A corporate retrieval team lands, ostensibly to assist his audit. Their leader, Director Hale, is courteous and menacing, offering Edmund promotion and transfer if he closes the file as clerical error. Beat: love against duty takes form—Edmund must choose what kind of man he is.

chapters.title: What the Dust Remembers
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo leads Edmund to the sealed habitat levels where the massacre happened, showing him scorch patterns and door codes only a witness would know. The memories hurt him physically when used. Beat: sacrifice of self to serve truth; bond between them deepens into something like family.

chapters.title: Blackwood, E.
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A personnel file surfaces with Edmund's own face and a service history on Vesper-9 he doesn't remember. His childhood, his mother's death, twenty years—all surgically edited. Beat: devastating reversal; the investigator discovers he is also evidence.

chapters.title: The Kindness of Forgetting
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, fragmented memory interludes. Flashbacks bleed through: a woman's laugh, a burning sky, a promise made to someone named Sera. He realizes the corporation didn't erase his past to hide the crime—it erased him because he was a witness who wouldn't stop talking. Beat: identity crisis; grief for a self he can't recover.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Hale reveals the full calculus: the massacre bought a mining rights settlement worth trillions; the erased records protect thousands of pensions and shareholders. He offers Edmund restoration of his memories—in exchange for Ivo. Beat: the central moral trap, stated plainly and temptingly.

chapters.title: Ivo Decides
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo overhears the offer and quietly prepares to surrender himself, believing his borrowed memories matter less than Edmund's real ones. He leaves a recorded confession as his legacy. Beat: heartbreaking loyalty; the child protecting the adult.

chapters.title: The Long Night of Records
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund refuses and goes underground in the colony's server vaults, racing to reconstruct the original telemetry before corporate wipe teams finish the job. Hale locks down the surface. Beat: rising tension; a siege of information rather than weapons.

chapters.title: Sera
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the vault he finds Sera's final log—his wife, a colony engineer who died sealing the doors, who hid the backup ledger inside the insurance claim that started everything. She sent it to him deliberately, trusting the man she knew he'd become. Beat: love across death; the emotional keystone of the book.

chapters.title: What We Buried Alive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Captured by Hale's team, Ivo endures interrogation, defending his memories as real because someone lived them, even if not him. Beat: endurance and dignity; the theme of loyalty vs. truth embodied in a child refusing to lie.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund hijacks the colony's long-range array to transmit the full record—ledger, telemetry, testimonies—to every relay in the system. Hale's team storms the vault. Beat: climax; the choice made irreversible, duty finally broken in favor of truth.

chapters.title: Echoes
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The broadcast lands: colonies erupt in protest, insurers freeze Halcyon Group assets, and Hale's cover collapses. But the wipe team reaches Edmund. Beat: triumph shadowed by loss; the truth is free but its messenger may not survive intact.

chapters.title: The Empty Chair
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, fading. Under wipe, Edmund loses names, faces, reasons—but clings to one anchor phrase Sera left him. He wakes with no past and a single instruction: find the boy. Beat: bittersweet sacrifice; identity traded for justice.

chapters.title: Someone Who Knew Him
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo, released in the chaos, finds Edmund blank-eyed in the ruined vault and tells him their story—every chapter of it—refusing to let the corporation win twice. Beat: tenderness; memory rebuilt through love rather than data.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Months later, Edmund testifies at the tribunal, his own erased history entered as evidence. He remembers nothing of Vesper-9 but speaks its 4,112 names from the ledger anyway. Beat: solemn resolution; truth institutionalized at personal cost.

chapters.title: The Garden Still Breathing
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ivo's shared POV. The two return to Vesper-9, now a memorial world, to plant the greenhouse seeds Sera saved. Edmund doesn't remember loving her, but he tends her garden. Beat: quiet healing; grief given somewhere to grow.

chapters.title: Ivo and the Echo
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, closing frame. Years later, Ivo, now a keeper of the colony archive, teaches new arrivals the names of the dead. Edmund visits each year, remembering a little more each time—or choosing to. Final beat: the echo outlives the silence; love and truth persist beyond memory itself.
